title: InfoQ AI, ML and Data Engineering Trends Report - 2026
gist: InfoQ's 2026 AI/ML/data engineering trends report (panel of Chip Huyen, Daniel Dominguez, Hien Luu, Arthur Casals) says 2026 is the year of inference and evaluations, agents are scaling from personal to organization-wide, and energy/infrastructure limits will shape 2027.

insights.claim: 2026 is called the year of inference, with inference expected to account for around two-thirds of AI compute spending by the end of this year.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Compute spend is shifting from training to serving; favors inference stacks, routing and memory/networking suppliers.
insights.quote: Inference is expected to account for around two-thirds of AI compute spending by the end of this year.

insights.claim: Reasoning models, long context and agents have turned inference from a model-execution problem into a systems problem spanning compute, memory, networking, routing and economics.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Value capture moves to the serving system, not only the model.

insights.claim: Open-weight models plus vLLM and SGLang make self-hosting approachable, with financial firms hosting internally for PII and others to cut coding costs.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Supports a growing on-prem/neocloud inference market and pressure on API pricing.
insights.locator: Hien Luu: The inference topic has exploded

insights.claim: System One models such as TypeSafe AI's Jev are expected to gain adoption for deterministic, faster and cheaper inference than LLMs.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Cheap decision models could displace LLM calls in agent loops.

insights.claim: Agents are moving from personal to team to organization-wide use, shifting AI from interface to an execution layer that plans, uses tools and works until a task completes.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Enterprise value is moving to operating agents at scale, boosting demand for orchestration, governance and observability.
insights.quote: AI is moving from being something that we interact [with] to something that we delegate [to].

insights.claim: 2025 was about learning to build agents; now organizations are working out how to operate, deploy and scale them in production.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Shift of spend from experimentation to ops tooling.
insights.locator: Similar to last year, Agentic AI

insights.claim: Agent SDKs from LangChain, Anthropic and OpenAI are expanding into harness engineering: memory management, code execution, file-system tools and hosted runtimes.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Platform vendors are bundling runtime layers, squeezing thin agent-framework startups.

insights.claim: Agent protocols such as MCP and A2A may become a new enterprise integration layer, with agent discovery sitting atop APIs.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Protocol standards are a potential choke point for integration vendors.

insights.claim: Context pollution, not window size, is the biggest context-engineering problem: more context can make an agent slower, more expensive and less reliable.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Retrieval quality and context governance matter more than larger windows.
insights.quote: more context can make an agent slower, more expensive, less reliable

insights.claim: 2026 is dubbed the year of AI evaluations; evaluating an agent means scoring task completion, cost, time, interventions and safety across model, tool, context and environment.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Eval harnesses are becoming a core go/no-go gate and a tooling category.
insights.locator: AI Evaluations for Models and Agents

insights.claim: Spec-driven development and AI software factories automate the SDLC from requirements to specs, tasks and generated code, with developers focusing on specifications.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Pushes AI deeper into the SDLC, raising the stakes on review and verification.
insights.locator: Spec-Driven Development and AI Software Factories

insights.claim: Physical AI mistakes carry physical consequences, making reliability, simulation, safety and verification more important, while robotics begins to adopt the foundation-model approach.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Evaluation and simulation tooling for robotics is an emerging niche.

insights.claim: Robot training cannot backtrack like LLM training: a robot that falls may break, and data scarcity is a second hurdle for companies like Generalist, Physical Intelligence, Sunday and Skild AI.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Robotics scaling depends on data strategy bets, and exploration cost is high.
insights.locator: One big difference between robotics, models, and LLMs

insights.claim: The panel expects AI growth to hit limits in electricity, capacity and data-center cooling, with 2027's biggest AI stories being energy, chips, infrastructure and geopolitics.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Power and siting constraints are a likely bottleneck for data-center buildout.

insights.claim: The panel expects more US robotics innovation, cheaper and faster models, every agent incorporating a Jev-style model, and smaller specialized agents for well-defined tasks.
insights.speaker: Srini Penchikala
insights.so_what: Directional predictions, not forecasts with numbers.
